resolvedQuestions.text: Q1: Which overlay-engine changes are required so a vendored repo whose overlay folder is `barter-overlays` can run status, apply and repin without an unexplained exit 2 or a whole-run abort on a protected path?

Q2: What do Barter's `barter-overlays` runbook, `overlay-manifest.json`, `replay.cjs`, `sync.cjs` and `sync-state.json` do that the Skilled engine does not, and what is the concrete migration path onto the engine's manifest and state schema?

Q3: Which runtime surfaces must be re-pinned or regenerated after a re-pin (dsh skill links, runtime mirrors, hook registrations, trigger index, advisor graph), and how should the engine express them?
Q4: Which root-file and cross-runtime traps (`AGENTS.md`, `REPO RULES.md`, `.opencode/scripts`, fork-drifted files) must the engine handle before an external repo can adopt it safely?
Q5: Which documentation and advertising changes are needed so adoption is discoverable and correctly described, and how should all proposed changes be ranked by impact and risk?

keyFindings.text: A missing `.skilled-overlays.json` does not itself fail status: `resolveOverlayDir` silently falls back to the literal folder `skilled-overlays`, and the run only dies one step later when `loadManifest` throws `no overlay manifest at …/overlay-manifest.json`, which the CLI catch turns into exit 2 with the message on stderr. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:375] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:425] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:3340]

The protected-path refusal is a whole-run throw, not a per-entry block: `assertSafeToPlan` raises for any `token`-named path it meets inside a directory or skill-root walk, and `analyze` raises again for a protected destination or source, so one `*token*` file aborts every other overlay's report with exit 2 and no `MISS` line naming the entry. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1688] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1801]

That throw is inconsistent with the engine's own reporting model: classified states in `BLOCKING_STATES` are printed per overlay as `blocked <overlay>: <state> <path>` and collected into the report, so an overlay-level refusal already has a shape the protected-path throw bypasses. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:58] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2884]

`DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FOLDERS` lists `.claude`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.devin`, `.opencode`, `.pi` and omits `.dsh`, while the doctor's own runtime-mirror contract treats `.dsh` as a first-class surface with `dsh_skills`, `dsh_prompts` and `dsh_agents` sync scripts, so a re-pin of a tree that ships `.dsh` mirrors copies stale mirrors unless the manifest overrides `repin.runtimeFolders`. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:74] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/tests/doctor-runtime-mirrors-contract.test.cjs:46]

A re-pin copies only `.skilled/**` plus the runtime folders and deletes only paths under `.skilled` and the runtime folders, so a root file such as `AGENTS.md` or `REPO RULES.md` is neither carried forward nor removed when upstream changes it; the vendored root copy silently drifts from the new pin. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2531] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2539]

`repin.exclude` already exists, is validated as a list of relative paths, and is covered by a test that keeps a real `.opencode/scripts` folder where upstream ships a link, so the brief's "no repin.exclude for .opencode/scripts" is a Barter manifest gap rather than a missing engine feature. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2503] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/tests/overlay-engine-repin.test.cjs:456]

Post-write regeneration is declared entirely by the manifest: `layoutLinks` recreate links, `regenerate` runs `argv` steps and snapshots their `outputs`, and `verifyGenerated` re-runs read-only checks with `fresh-true` or `zero-changed` expectations, so dsh skill links, runtime mirrors, hook registrations, trigger index and advisor graph can all be re-pinned today only if a manifest names them; the engine ships no default step set. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1424] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1516] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1531]

A staged re-pin deliberately drops the regenerate and verify blocks before writing the copy, so a clean `RESULT: STAGED` report is not evidence that the live post-repin tree regenerated or verified. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2914]

Barter's `replay.cjs` and `sync.cjs` are a fork of the Skilled overlay engine rather than an independent tool: the WHY preamble is the same text about a vendored tree being replaced wholesale, and the shared function names (`planOverlay`, `assertSafeToPlan`, `classifyDestination`, `commandGuard`) match the engine's, so adoption is an upstreaming problem, not a replatform. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/replay.cjs:4] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:106]

Barter's fork adds a sixth destination state, `fork-drifted`, fed by `upstreamSource` metadata that two entries carry, so a Barter fork of an upstream file stays visible and non-blocking; the engine's `STATUS_NAMES` has five states and never reads `upstreamSource`, so both forks become invisible after migration. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:17] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:402] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:67]

The token-name refusal differs in exactly the way that breaks `barter-design-tokens.md`: Barter's fork allows `.md`, `.css`, `.ts` and `.svelte` names, while the engine refuses any basename containing `token` that is not named exactly by the manifest. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:91] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1555]

No Barter entry declares `protectedPaths` (0 of 130), so the migration fix for that file is manifest-side: `references/barter-design-tokens.md` added to the `repo-frontend` directory entry's `protectedPaths`, which the engine accepts because it resolves the value relative to the entry. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1595]

Barter's `sk-git` skill-root entry declares 16 `outsideCertificate` paths with a reason each, and its fork validates and honors them as intentionally vendor-owned; the engine has no reader for `outsideCertificate`, so every exemption those paths carry is lost on migration. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/replay.cjs:813] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2337]

Barter's `sync-state.json` is already the engine's state shape (`schemaVersion: 1`, `pin`, `files` with 454 destination hashes), so it can seed an engine state file directly, but the engine will only look for that file inside the folder named by `.skilled-overlays.json` (or the literal `skilled-overlays`), and Barter ships neither the setting nor a `skilled-overlays` folder. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync-state.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:375] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:430]

Barter has no re-pin command at all: neither script mentions `repin`, and the re-pin is an eight-step hand runbook that copies seven runtime folders including `.dsh`, excludes `.opencode/scripts`, then regenerates dsh skill links, runtime mirrors, hook registrations, the trigger index and the advisor graph, and finally compares a Barter fork of the git skill. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/README.md:90] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/README.md:108] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2914]

Barter's edit guard is a different core from Skilled's `overlay-guard`: it spawns `sync.cjs` from the overlay folder and layers a separate session gate, while Skilled's guard allows immediately unless `.skilled-overlays.json` or `skilled-overlays/` exists at the tree root, so today it is inert in Barter and after adoption two guards would run over the same writes. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/.skilled/hooks/overlay-sync/lib/overlay-sync-core.cjs:11] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/overlay-guard/lib/overlay-guard.cjs:32] [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/overlay-guard/lib/overlay-guard.cjs:111]

Barter's own documentation has already drifted from its manifest: the vendored `README.md` still pins `23b4f3d2e7` while `overlay-manifest.json` and `sync-state.json` both carry `230d22ba88`, which is the same silent-drift class the engine's own status check cannot see because it never reads a README. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/README.md:9] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1]

Barter's manifest already declares a `hook-registrations` pair — a regenerate step and its `--check` verify — pointing at `sync-hook-registrations.cjs`, so the brief's list is wrong on that item: hook registration regeneration is expressible and already expressed. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1394] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1502]

The dsh skill sync is a clean regenerate/verify pair the engine can express today — `sync-skills-dsh.cjs` writes without flags and `--check` reports `MISSING`/`STALE`/`EXTRA` drift and returns 1 — yet Barter's manifest never names it, so `expect: "exit-0"` on `--check` would close the brief's dsh-link gap with no engine change. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dsh/sync-skills-dsh.cjs:46] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dsh/sync-skills-dsh.cjs:317]

`sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs` follows the same shape — no flag writes, `--check` collects `STALE`/`MISSING`/`EXTRA` drift and exits non-zero — so runtime-mirror regeneration is also a manifest entry, not an engine feature. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/runtime-mirrors/sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs:70] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/runtime-mirrors/sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs:317]

The trigger index already has the exact `fresh-true` contract the engine's `verifyGenerated` expects: `generate-trigger-index.mjs --check --json` returns a `fresh` boolean and exits 1 when a document is stale or the corpus is untrusted, so regeneration plus freshness is one manifest pair. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs:33] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs:565]

The advisor graph is the one surface the engine cannot fully express: rebuilding is `skill-advisor.cjs advisor_rebuild` (operator-gated, no freshness output), and the only checkable surface is `skill-graph-freshness.cjs`, which is report-only, exits 0 by default, and gates only under `--strict`; so a manifest can only pair an `advisor_rebuild` regenerate step with a `skill-graph-freshness.cjs --strict` exit-0 verify, never a `fresh-true` expectation. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/skill-graph-freshness.cjs:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/skill-graph-freshness.cjs:20]

The re-pin workflow's own invariant claims the stage runs every step on a copy, but the engine deliberately strips `regenerate` and `verifyGenerated` from a staged run, so a clean `RESULT: STAGED` report can precede a live re-pin whose regeneration fails; the two contracts disagree and the stage report carries no line saying regeneration was skipped. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-overlay-repin.yaml:40] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2914]

Regeneration steps are arbitrary argv run with `cwd` at the tree root and no allowlist, so a vendored repo's manifest is an execution surface: whoever writes `manifest.regenerate` decides what a re-pin runs, which is why a migration should copy a reviewed step list rather than accept one from an untrusted overlay folder. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1478] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1531]

Doctor already treats the dsh surfaces as first-class mirrors, with `dsh_skills`, `dsh_prompts` and `dsh_agents` scripted against `.dsh/skills`, `.dsh/prompts` and `.dsh/agents`, so a re-pin that omits `.dsh` from its runtime folders contradicts the doctor model, not just Barter's runbook. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/tests/doctor-runtime-mirrors-contract.test.cjs:46]

`.opencode/scripts` needs no engine change: the engine already refuses a folder where upstream ships a file with a message that names the fix (`list it in repin.exclude to keep it`), and refuses unowned drift with `move each edit into an overlay, list the path in repin.exclude, or restore it from <pin>`, so Barter's `tar --exclude .opencode/scripts` becomes a manifest `repin.exclude` entry. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2671] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2969] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/README.md:94]

The engine refuses when the overlay folder sits inside a folder a re-pin copies, and Barter's `barter-overlays/` sits at the tree root outside `.skilled` and the runtime folders, so `.skilled-overlays.json` naming it is the only missing piece for adoption — no engine change is needed for placement. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2961] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1]

Root files are structurally outside the re-pin copy and delete sets, which makes Barter's documented whole-archive trap impossible through the engine, but the same exclusion means an upstream change to a root file is never applied and no report line says so; the reference doc states `Root files such as AGENTS.md are never copied` as a fact rather than as a warning that those changes are dropped. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2531] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/README.md:186] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-doctor/references/overlays.md:120]

`AGENTS.md` and `REPO RULES.md` have a second owner: `/doctor:agents-md check` reports twelve rows including `REPO RULES.md`, so after a re-pin two commands own the same root files and neither the router docs nor the reference states which one wins. [SOURCE: README.md:1452] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2531]

`.dsh` is treated inconsistently inside Skilled itself: the overlay guard ships a dsh adapter, so dsh edits are protected, while the engine's default runtime folder list omits `.dsh`, so dsh mirrors are skipped on re-pin unless the manifest overrides `repin.runtimeFolders`. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/overlay-guard/dsh/overlay-guard.mjs:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:74]

The advertised install route never mentions overlays: `/doctor:install` has zero overlay mentions, and the install, setup and helper workflow assets have none either, while root README section 5 documents `status`, `apply`, `--capture` and `repin` in full — so a repo that follows the install path never discovers the feature it needs. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/install.md:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-install.yaml:1] [SOURCE: README.md:300]

The overlays reference already documents the setting, `protectedPaths` with the literal `references/barter-design-tokens.md` example, `repin.exclude` and the root-file rule, so the brief's "docs only advertise linking" is false for that file; what is genuinely missing is adoption guidance for a repo that already has a hand-rolled overlay folder, manifest extensions and a state file. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-doctor/references/overlays.md:44] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-doctor/references/overlays.md:92] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skilled-doctor/references/overlays.md:120]

Fork-drifted tracking has no engine and no documentation expression: Barter's fork adds the state and validates `outsideCertificate` reasons, while the engine ignores both keys, so a migrating repo deletes those declarations and loses the only visibility it had into upstream-vs-fork divergence. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:402] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/replay.cjs:813] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:67]

Ranked engine change P1 — make a protected path a per-entry refusal instead of a whole-run throw: `assertSafeToPlan` and `analyze` currently raise before any report exists, while `BLOCKING_STATES`/`reportBlocked` already give every other refusal a per-overlay line, so moving the protected check into that reporting path fixes a confusing exit 2 with no new state. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1688] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1801] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2884]

Ranked engine change P2 — add `.dsh` to `DEFAULT_RUNTIME_FOLDERS`: the doctor's runtime-mirror contract already treats `.dsh` as three first-class surfaces (`dsh_skills`, `dsh_prompts`, `dsh_agents`), and a re-pin that skips it leaves stale dsh mirrors; the change also touches the repin tests' hard-coded `copy N paths` expectations, which must be re-baselined. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:74] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/tests/doctor-runtime-mirrors-contract.test.cjs:46] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/tests/overlay-engine-repin.test.cjs:280]

Ranked engine change P3 — make a stage report state that regeneration and verification were skipped: the engine strips both blocks for a staged run and prints nothing about it, while the re-pin workflow's invariant claims the stage runs every step on a copy, so one printed line plus the workflow text correction closes a real expectation gap. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2914] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-overlay-repin.yaml:40]

Ranked engine change P4 — report upstream root-file changes the re-pin excludes: the copy and delete sets are built only from `.skilled` and the runtime folders, so an upstream change to `AGENTS.md` or `REPO RULES.md` is never applied and never named, even though `/doctor:agents-md` reports rows for both files and the two writers have no documented precedence. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2531] [SOURCE: README.md:1452]

Ranked engine change P5 — make a missing overlay setting diagnosable: today the fallback to `skilled-overlays` turns "no setting and no such folder" into `no overlay manifest at skilled-overlays/overlay-manifest.json`, which reads like a corrupt manifest; a distinct "no overlay folder named" message, or a guarded search for any folder holding `overlay-manifest.json`, fixes the adoption path without touching classification. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:375] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:425]

Ranked engine change P6/P7 — `fork-drifted` and `outsideCertificate` are one optional extension, not two: both exist only in Barter's fork, both are non-blocking visibility features, and the engine's five-state classifier plus its skill-root planner would each need a new branch, so they should ship together behind one documented manifest contract or not at all. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/sync.cjs:17] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/replay.cjs:813] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:67]

Declined engine change — extension-based token trust: Barter's fork allows `.md`, `.css`, `.ts` and `.svelte` names, but adopting that rule would weaken the engine's secret-file posture for every consumer; `protectedPaths` already gives a per-path, path-relative opt-in and the reference doc publishes it with the exact Barter example, so the manifest fix is preferred over the heuristic fix. ruledOutDirections.text: Running `overlay-engine.cjs status` against this repo to observe the failure: the engine writes nothing in status mode, but a run would still need the repo's own setting and manifest, and the finding is fully derivable from the branches; the command was not run to keep the write surface clean.
Looking for an engine-level default regeneration list: there is none; the only default is the runtime folder list, which is the `.dsh` gap in finding 4.
Looking for a "setting file missing" diagnostic: none exists, so an operator sees a manifest-path error instead of a settings error, which explains the confusing exit 2 in the brief.

Reading the engine's usage header as the contract: the header documents exit codes per command but not the `.skilled-overlays.json` fallback or the protected-path throw, and both were only visible in the function bodies (lines 375-379, 1688-1703).
Treating the brief's gap list as authoritative: finding 6 directly contradicts it, so the brief was demoted to hypotheses and re-verified item by item.

Treating Barter's scripts as an unrelated bespoke implementation: the shared preamble and function names make that untenable, and it changes the recommendation from "replace Barter's tool" to "upstream its deltas".
Searching for a `repin` implementation inside Barter: none, by design; the runbook is the implementation.

Assuming the manifest would need rewriting from scratch: 130 entries, 19 layout links, 9 regenerate steps and 10 verify steps already match the engine's schema; only `outsideCertificate`, `upstreamSource` and the missing `pin.checkout` reader are engine-side gaps.
Looking for `protectedPaths` in Barter's manifest to explain the design-tokens refusal: it is absent everywhere, so the refusal comes from the engine's name heuristic, not from a malformed entry.

Assuming the advisor graph can be treated like the others: the rebuild has no read-only freshness mode, so it must be a regenerate step plus a separate report-only gate, and that asymmetry has to be documented rather than papered over.
Assuming the engine needs a new regeneration mechanism: three of the five surfaces (dsh links, runtime mirrors, trigger index) are expressible with manifest entries the engine already supports.
Looking for an advisor freshness JSON contract: `skill-graph-freshness.cjs` prints a panel, not a `fresh` field, so the `fresh-true` expectation cannot be reused there.
Looking for an engine-level "post-repin hook": none; `regenerate` runs inside `applyUnderLock` after the copy, which is the post-repin point, so no new hook is needed.
Trusting the repin workflow's stage invariant: the engine's stage branch contradicts it, so the workflow text needs the correction, not just the engine.
Expecting the engine to need a root-file copy rule: the exclusion is deliberate and correct for a re-pin; the gap is the missing report line and the missing precedence rule, not the exclusion.
Searching `update.md`, `symlink.md`, `runtime-mirrors.md` and `env.md` for overlay mentions: zero in each, which confirms the discovery gap is route-level rather than a single missing sentence.
Looking for a documented precedence between `/doctor:agents-md` and the overlay engine over `AGENTS.md`: none exists.
Expecting the docs to be silent about overlays: root README section 5 and the reference are thorough, so the fix is routing and adoption guidance rather than writing the feature up from scratch.
Expecting `.opencode/scripts` and `.dsh` to be engine features: both are manifest configuration plus defaults, and only the defaults need to change.
Treating the `.dsh` default as a documentation-only change: the repin tests assert exact copy counts, so it is a code + test change with a doc note.
Looking for a test that would catch a missing `.dsh` default: the engine tests do not enumerate the default list, only the doctor mirror contract does.
